skill.name: stride-analysis-patterns
skill.description: Apply STRIDE methodology to systematically identify threats. Use when analyzing system security, conducting threat modeling sessions, or creating security documentation.
skill.summary: Apply STRIDE threat modeling patterns to identify, document, and prioritize security threats.
skill.author: wshobson

content.value_statement: Security reviews often miss threats when teams rely on informal checklists. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured STRIDE templates for consistent threat identification.
actual_capabilities: Provides STRIDE category questions for spoofing, tampering, repudiation, information disclosure, denial of service, and elevation of privilege.
Includes a threat model document template with assets, trust boundaries, risks, mitigations, and recommendations.
Offers Python examples for organizing threats, scoring risk, and generating threat summaries.
Maps data flow diagram elements to relevant STRIDE threat categories.
Supports per-interaction analysis for component-to-component communication paths.
Lists practical mitigations for each STRIDE category.
limitations: It does not inspect live systems or automatically verify implemented controls.
The Python snippets are examples and may need adaptation before operational use.
Threat likelihood and impact still require human judgment and system context.
It does not replace penetration testing, secure code review, or compliance validation.

use_cases.title: Review a New Architecture
use_cases.description: Use the templates to identify STRIDE threats before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Document Application Risks
use_cases.description: Create a threat model with assets, trust boundaries, ranked risks, and mitigation actions.

use_cases.title: Teach Threat Modeling
use_cases.description: Use the category questions and examples to guide team workshops.

prompt_templates.title: Start a STRIDE Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review for a known system
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply STRIDE to this system description. Identify threats by category, affected assets, likely impact, and basic mitigations.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Trust Boundaries
prompt_templates.scenario: Architecture review with a data flow diagram
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these components, data flows, and trust boundaries. List threats for each boundary crossing and explain the STRIDE category.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Threats
prompt_templates.prompt: Rank these STRIDE threats by likelihood and impact. Explain the top risks and recommend immediate, short-term, and long-term actions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Complete Threat Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Produce a complete threat model for this architecture using STRIDE. Include assets, assumptions, trust boundaries, threats, mitigations, owners, and review questions.

output_examples.input: A public web app sends user requests through an API gateway to internal services and a database.
output_examples.output: The review identifies spoofing risks at login, tampering risks at API inputs, information disclosure risks at the database, and denial-of-service risks at public endpoints.

output_examples.input: A payment service writes audit events and stores transaction records in separate systems.
output_examples.output: The model highlights repudiation risks around audit integrity, tampering risks for transaction updates, and mitigation steps such as signed logs and strict authorization.

output_examples.input: A team has a data flow diagram with external users, services, stores, and several trust boundaries.
output_examples.output: The analysis maps each element to STRIDE categories and calls out unencrypted boundary crossings as high-priority review items.

best_practices: Start with assets, trust boundaries, and data flows before listing threats.
Record assumptions and evidence for likelihood and impact ratings.
Assign owners and due dates to each accepted mitigation.
anti_patterns: Using STRIDE as a checkbox exercise without architecture context.
Listing threats without mitigations, owners, or review dates.
Ignoring low-likelihood threats when the impact is severe.

faq.question: What is STRIDE?
faq.answer: STRIDE is a threat modeling method covering spoofing, tampering, repudiation, information disclosure, denial of service, and elevation of privilege.

faq.question: Does this skill run security scans?
faq.answer: No. It provides templates, questions, and examples for structured threat modeling.

faq.question: Can it analyze data flow diagrams?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes patterns for mapping data flow elements and trust boundary crossings to STRIDE categories.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Security architects, application security engineers, developers, and engineering leaders can use it during design reviews.

faq.question: Does it provide remediation guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It lists common mitigations for each STRIDE category and supports prioritized action planning.

faq.question: Is it enough for compliance signoff?
faq.answer: No. It can support documentation, but compliance signoff requires organization-specific evidence and approval.
